metadata.purpose: R10 probe: plugin:java-controller mount + the D9 security wrapper. Two mounted @RestControllers from the definition directory, deliberately gated at different roles so ONE probe proves both directions -- the mount actually serves a request, AND minimumRole enforcement genuinely rejects an under-privileged caller. adminTools is minimumRole=ADMIN, which the dev/auth.mode=none profile auto-grants every caller (CLAUDE.md's agent-proxy precedent), so it proves the ACCEPT path. superOnlyTools is minimumRole=SUPERUSER, which that same dev fallback NEVER grants (CLAUDE.md: 'ADMIN is no gate at all in dev apps ... SUPERUSER is never in that fallback set') -- the identical dev-key caller that succeeds against adminTools must be rejected here, proving the wrapper checks the DECLARED role and not just 'is authenticated'.
